coordinates.note: MACE position 32 deg 46 min 46 s N, 78 deg 58 min 35 s E from the MACE sensitivity paper, converted to decimal degrees. HAGAR is described as being on the same site (arXiv:2406.15037) but no source gives a separate HAGAR coordinate, so both experiments use this point.
coordinates.quote: Hanle in Ladakh, India (32^0 46^' 46^" N, 78^0 58^' 35^" E) at an altitude of 4270 m a.s.l.

name: Hanle gamma-ray telescope site (MACE and HAGAR)
notes: Altitude sources vary: 4270 m (MACE and HAGAR papers), 4300 m (arXiv:1110.6795) and 4500 m (arXiv:2406.15037); the 4270 m of the instrument papers is used.

summary.plain: A high mountain site at Hanle in Ladakh, northern India, about 4270 metres up, where two Indian gamma-ray telescopes, the HAGAR array and the 21 m MACE telescope, observe the TeV sky.
summary.technical: Hanle (Ladakh, Himalayas), 4270 m a.s.l.: site of the HAGAR wavefront-sampling array (2008) and the 21 m MACE imaging Cherenkov telescope (2021), the highest-altitude Cherenkov telescopes in the world.
